university-of-kansas.faculty: Sarah Deer, University Distinguished Professor of Law (with joint appointments in Women, Gender & Sexuality Studies and Public Affairs & Administration), is a 2014 MacArthur Fellow recognized for her work on tribal law and violence against Native women; she joined KU after the fellowship, and her MacArthur-era affiliation (William Mitchell College of Law) is no longer current. Steven Prohira, assistant professor of physics and astronomy and principal investigator of the Radar Echo Telescope project, is a 2022 MacArthur Fellow for his work detecting ultra-high energy neutrinos. Faculty rosters change; verify current status before citing.

research.level: R1 ("very high research activity") and one of 71 institutions in the Association of American Universities; KU reported $610.6 million in research and development expenditures in FY25 across five strategic research themes (development across the lifespan; earth, energy and environment; the human experience in the digital age; molecules and medicines; and security and safety).
research.undergrad: The Center for Undergraduate Research & Fellowships (CURF) supports students across all disciplines with Undergraduate Research Awards ($1,000 grants for original research or creative projects under a KU faculty mentor), course-based research funding, peer research ambassadors, and campus presentation events.
research.areas: Signature strengths include the Radar Echo Telescope astroparticle physics project led by MacArthur Fellow Steven Prohira and the university's broader push, branded "Research Rising," to expand faculty capacity in its five strategic themes.

research.level: Classified Research 2 ("High Research Spending and Doctorate Production") under the Carnegie Classification.
research.undergrad: The Office of Research for Undergraduates coordinates faculty-mentored research and creative projects across all colleges, and Miami hosts NSF-funded Research Experiences for Undergraduates (REU) sites, including a 10-week summer program in Ecology in Human Dominated Landscapes and a Summer REU in Chemistry and Biochemistry.
research.areas: Miami's research identity centers on undergraduate-embedded scholarship rather than large sponsored-research volume, with the ecology and chemistry/biochemistry REU sites its most externally visible NSF-funded programs.

research.level: K-State reported $264.9 million in research and development expenditures and holds 400+ active patents, with more than 90 research centers and institutes across campus.
research.undergrad: Undergraduates engage in research through faculty-mentored projects coordinated by the university's research division, spanning agriculture, engineering, and the sciences.
research.areas: K-State's research identity is closely tied to its land-grant mission, with particular strength in agriculture, plant and animal biosecurity, and applied engineering.

research.level: Carnegie R1 ("very high research activity"); UW received $221 million in sponsored funding in FY25 and has ranked among the top 100 U.S. universities for patent production for two consecutive years.
research.undergrad: Students engage through Undergraduate Research & Inquiry Day (URID), coordinated through the EPSCoR office, alongside access to the Advanced Research Computing Center and campus research labs.
research.areas: Named research centers include the High Plains American Indian Research Institute and the Wyoming Institute for Humanities Research, reflecting UW's regional strengths in natural resources, energy, and the humanities of the American West.

research.level: PSU brands itself "Oregon's Urban Research University" and reported $73.7 million in research expenditures for FY2024, with major federal support from NIH, NSF, and the U.S. Department of Education.
research.undergrad: The university emphasizes community-embedded and applied projects — framed institutionally as work with "tangible, lasting benefits" for the Portland region — with support available through campus research centers, the Business Accelerator, and the Center for Entrepreneurship.
research.areas: PSU's signature research focus is urban and public-impact scholarship: transportation (including sustainable and equitable transportation research), urban development, and environmental challenges facing the Portland metro area.

research.level: ODU reported $89.6 million in sponsored research awards and $116 million in research and development expenditures for FY2025, across 927 active awards, with more than half of faculty involved in funded research.
research.undergrad: Undergraduates join funded projects sponsored by federal agencies and industry partners alongside graduate students.
research.areas: ODU's stated nationally known research strengths are coastal resilience, modeling and simulation, bioelectrics, cybersecurity, and port logistics/maritime engineering — reflecting its Hampton Roads location alongside major military and port infrastructure.

research.level: A specialized art and design school (BFA/MFA) now operating as a division of Willamette University since a 2021 merger; scholarly activity is organized around studio-based creative practice and critical/visual studies rather than sponsored scientific research.
research.undergrad: Undergraduates work directly in studio practice across 11 BFA concentrations (including Painting and Drawing, Sculpture, Photography, Printmaking, Illustration, and Graphic Design), culminating in a BFA senior thesis exhibition; graduate students can pursue teaching assistantships and fellowships in the Hallie Ford School of Graduate Studies.
research.areas: PNCA's distinction is its studio-intensive BFA/MFA model and small scale (roughly 650 total students, a 9-to-1 student-to-faculty ratio) rather than sponsored research output.

research.level: Carnegie R1 ("very high research activity") doctoral university.
research.undergrad: UNM states that research opportunities extend "from undergraduate research to sponsored faculty projects".
research.areas: UNM's research infrastructure includes the Center for High Technology Materials (CHTM), the Clinical & Translational Science Center (CTSC), the Center for Advanced Research Computing (CARC), and the Center for Quantum Information and Control (CQuIC).

university-of-kentucky.faculty: Loka Ashwood, associate professor of sociology, is a 2024 MacArthur Fellow recognized for her work on how environmental issues, corporate interests, and state policy intersect to harm rural communities and erode trust in democracy; she joined UK after prior faculty positions elsewhere (most recently Auburn University), and per the MacArthur Foundation's own listing she is currently based at UK. Note: an earlier MacArthur-fellow artist sometimes associated with UK's faculty in web searches (Ebony G. Patterson) is described in sourcing as a past, not current, instructor and is excluded here. Faculty rosters change; verify current status before citing.

research.level: Carnegie R1 ("very high research activity") institution.
research.undergrad: The Office of Undergraduate Research (OUR), founded in 2009, has served more than 9,000 students and administers named funding programs including the Commonwealth Undergraduate Research Experience (CURE) Fellowship, the Beckman Scholars Program, the Oswald Competition, Sustainability Research Fellowships, and a Work-Study Research Assistant Program; UK students have made 762 presentations at the National Conference on Undergraduate Research.

research.level: Classified Research 2 ("Doctoral Institution — High Research Activity") under the Carnegie Classification.
research.undergrad: TSU offers a named Undergraduate Research Experiences program supported by campus Centers of Excellence and Seed Grant Awards.
research.areas: Stated research focus areas include agricultural sciences and biotechnology, engineering and nanomaterials, health sciences, cybersecurity and artificial intelligence, and astrophysics.
